lane_comparison.question_asked: do research/g3-scoped-failure-memory-v1 (main) and research/g3-real-failure-v1 (cursor) contradict, overlap, or is one a strict refinement of the other?

g3_scoped_failure_memory_v1_on_main.measures: whether counterexamples encountered by the existing polynomial synthesizer produce reusable scoped failure-point records that save repeated interpreter work on later tasks, survive a real process restart, and lose exactly that effect after production evidence withdrawal
g3_scoped_failure_memory_v1_on_main.self_framing: ordinary checked memoization / counterexample reuse, explicitly not a novel OCM algorithm; the equally equipped conventional parent gets identical records, checking, lookup and solver; a tie is PARENT_SUFFICIENT

g3_scoped_failure_memory_v1_on_main.status: REGISTERED, NOT YET REPORTING A RESULT

g3_real_failure_v1_on_cursor.measures: whether a specific source + evidence_id incident is recoverable from the production ledger after OS-process restart or a new solve episode
g3_real_failure_v1_on_cursor.self_framing: its own CORE.md states the obligation is different, and that the incident must be a specific evidence/source identity 'not from a task-id cache'

lane_comparison.verdict: NO CONTRADICTION AND NEITHER IS A REFINEMENT. Different keys and different outcome variables: work saved by failure-point memoization versus recoverability of a provenance-bound incident. They also never coexisted - the cursor G3 family is g3-failure-memory-v1, g3-real-failure-v1, g3-representation-v1 and g3-representation-diagnosis-v1, and never contained g3-scoped-failure-memory-v1. No supersession decision is required.
lane_comparison.note_on_naming: The near-collision g3-failure-memory-v1 (cursor) against g3-scoped-failure-memory-v1 (main) is what makes these look like competing lanes. They are not the same capsule.
